name: Sorting network on 27 inputs
description: Construct a sorting network on 27 wires with as few comparators as possible. A comparator (i, j) with i < j compares the values on wires i and j and puts the smaller one on wire i and the larger one on wire j; the comparators are applied in the given order. The network must sort every input, that is, leave the values in non-decreasing order along wires 0 to 26.

sources.locator: Using Symmetry and Evolutionary Search to Minimize Sorting Networks
Codish et al. (2015), Sorting Networks: to the End and Back Again: new networks for 17 to 20 inputs, mainly about depth (layers), so not evidence for the size objective.
Ehlers and Mueller (2014), Faster Sorting Networks for 17, 19 and 20 Inputs: depth upper bounds, not size.
Depth-13 Sorting Networks for 28 Channels (2025): depth upper bounds for 27 and 28 inputs, not size.

execution.interface: construct() -> list of comparators (i, j) with 0 <= i < j < 27, in the order in which they are applied (at least one). The network is verified on all 2^27 inputs of zeros and ones, which is equivalent to sorting every input. Score: number of comparators, minimized (the depth is not scored).

limitations: Exact 0-1 verification over all 2^27 inputs, in blocks of 2^24; one evaluation takes a few seconds for n = 30 and up to about half a minute for n = 32.
SorterHunter and symmetry-based searches have worked on these sizes for years.
The record was reproduced by this task's verifier from a published solution (or an optimiser run). See VALIDITY.md.

checks: smallest listed network for n=27 has 147 comparators, depth 16
sorts every input (exact check by our verifier)

science_relevance.reason: Valsalam and Miikkulainen's main objective is the comparator count of sorting networks with up to 32 inputs, which is exactly what the task scores; the record itself comes from Dobbelaere's SorterHunter-based list, which is a web page and not a paper, so only one paper qualifies and the status rests on it.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Construct a sorting network on 27 wires with as few comparators as possible.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Sorting networks are oblivious sorting procedures used in hardware, SIMD and GPU sorting, and the minimum number of comparators is known only for up to 12 inputs; for 13 and more inputs the best known sizes are upper bounds that have been lowered by evolutionary and SAT searches, so a smaller network is a new upper bound.

papers.title: Using Symmetry and Evolutionary Search to Minimize Sorting Networks
papers.task_relation: The paper treats the same size-minimisation problem up to 32 inputs: its Table 2 lists the then best known sizes for 17 to 32 inputs and its abstract reports new minimal networks for 17 to 22 inputs and ties for larger n. The task's 27-input records (Dobbelaere's list) are lower than the paper's for 19 to 29 inputs and equal for 30 to 32; the paper is not the source of the current record.
papers.primary_goal: Minimise the number of comparators of sorting networks with a method combining problem symmetry and evolutionary search (SENSO).
